title: The Great Rupert

evidence.note: Wikipedia states the film entered the public domain in 1978 when its 28-year copyright term lapsed without renewal. That is a secondary claim. No Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volume or Copyright Office record was retrieved in this session, so non-renewal is not established here. The Internet Archive item carries a Public Domain Mark 1.0 license tag, which is an uploader label and not a rights record.

The recorded soundtrack of a sound film normally shares the film's own copyright status, so the score likely follows the print. Neither the print nor any separate score registration or renewal has been verified.
Wikipedia says the Ted Allan story was also published as a children's book, Willie the Squowse. The book's publication date and any renewal of its copyright were not verified in this session.

In 2003, 20th Century Fox and Legend Films released a colorized version titled A Christmas Wish, with an audio commentary by Terry Moore. Colorization and added commentary can carry their own copyright. A faithful copy of the black-and-white original adds none.

editorial:
The Great Rupert (1950) is an American comedy-fantasy produced by George Pal and directed by Irving Pichel, with Jimmy Durante, Tom Drake and Terry Moore. Rupert is a squirrel, animated in stop-motion. The screenplay is by László Vadnay, from an original story by Ted Allan.

Wikipedia reports that the film entered the public domain in 1978, when its 28-year term lapsed without renewal. This dossier could not confirm that from the renewal records, so treat the print as unverified until you check the Catalog of Copyright Entries and the Copyright Office catalog yourself. Two layers are open. The Ted Allan story also appeared as a children's book, Willie the Squowse, and its status is unchecked. The 2003 colorized release from Fox and Legend Films, titled A Christmas Wish, may be protected separately, so source a black-and-white print.
faq: Is The Great Rupert free to use?

It is reported as being in the public domain since 1978, but this dossier did not verify that against the renewal records. The story, which also appeared as the book Willie the Squowse, and the score were not checked either. Check the 1977 to 1979 renewal records before relying on it.
Can I use the colorized A Christmas Wish version?
Not safely. The 2003 colorization released by Fox and Legend Films, with a Terry Moore commentary, may carry its own copyright. Use a black-and-white copy of the original instead.
